mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off channel, lowering near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening episodes are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signal disinflation, which reduces policy rate expectations and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months below its prior month's value
failure_condition: Over 100 similar three-month disinflation episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during ongoing inflationary periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs per month indicates a labor market recovery that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 50,000 by at least 20,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: In 10 similar labor market acceleration events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than in pre-recession periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior quarter's median, accompanied by a decline in retail sales proxy (HOUST), signals weakening aggregate demand that depresses equity risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prior quarter median AND HOUST < prior quarter median
failure_condition: In 5 analogous demand contraction episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during baseline growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in manufacturing capacity utilization (not directly observable but proxy via INDPRO) combined with a sustained drop in raw material prices (not directly observable but implied by INDPRO behavior) suggests supply-side easing that supports equity valuations, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months below its prior month's value
regime_hint: supply-chain easing in a tight-labor environment
failure_condition: Across 10 analogous supply easing episodes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during supply shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals a cooling labor market, which increases perceived risk and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% by at least 0.5 percentage points
regime_hint: early stage of labor market cooling
failure_condition: In 8 similar labor market cooling episodes, 5-day forward returns are not more negative than during stable employment periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) below their respective 5-period moving averages indicates a dual-demand shock that depresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 7 analogous dual-demand shocks, 20-day forward returns are not more negative than during single-demand shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of very low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 205 for three consecutive months) combined with a persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) creates a 'soft landing' expectation that reduces term premium and supports equity prices, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 205 for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 similar low-inflation/low-rate regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during moderate inflation/high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).
